content:
maria: Heads-up: around 06:40 UTC we saw a spike in 5xx errors for internal inference routing in eu-west. Traces show a lot of gRPC timeouts with `context deadline exceeded` when calling model-proxy -> model-router. I'm seeing CoreDNS latency spikes and a bunch of DNS timeouts.
ashok: yup saw that too. kube-dns latency graph jumped from ~5ms to 300-500ms for ~15m. Node-local-dns pods on some nodes are reporting errors. Could be packet loss between node-local-dns and coredns.
lee: any change deployments or infra churn around that time? autoscaler, rolling kernel updates?
maria: no large rollouts. We did have a scheduled node-maintenance earlier in the night but that ended before the spike. Also interesting: GPU nodes using SR-IOV RDMA path show unusual counters on mlx5 NICs at ~06:38. Not sure if relates.
kelsey: dns-bot alerted: `CoreDNS pod coredns-5d8f6 failed backoff` on three nodes. node-local-dns DS had 2/3 pods not ready in eu-west-zone-b.
ashok: quick triage steps I ran: 1) `kubectl -n kube-system get pods -o wide | grep node-local-dns` 2) `kubectl logs -n kube-system node-local-dns-xxxx` 3) tcpdump to see DNS packet loss. Example: 
```
kubectl -n kube-system exec -it node-local-dns-xxxx -- tcpdump -n -i any udp port 53 -c 200
# saw ~12% UDP retransmits and many truncated responses
```
ashok: Also ran `dig @127.0.0.53 model-router.default.svc.cluster.local +time=2 +tries=1` from affected pods and got `;; WARNING: recursion requested but not available` and a bunch of timeouts.
lee: that recursion warning usually means node-local-dns is trying to recurse but upstream is flapping. Is CoreDNS overloaded or failing cluster-internal queries?
maria: checked CoreDNS metrics: `coredns_request_duration_seconds` p50 -> 8ms normally, p95 jumped to 420ms, and `coredns_dns_request_count_total` dropped on some replicas (they were OOMKilled). Logs show repeated `read udp ...: i/o timeout`.
kelsey: speculating: MTU mismatch on overlay or host NIC causing fragmentation and UDP DNS packets being dropped. Also RDMA NICs with offload might bypass iptables/overlay path and create fragmentation differences.
ashok: good point. I ran `ip -s link show` on affected nodes: many had RX errors and `mtu 9000` while most others are 1500. A few nodes were configured for jumbo frames (9000) after an older upgrade and that mismatched the calico veths -> causes fragmentation.
maria: that explains UDP frag issues. Short-term mitigation: 1) restart node-local-dns DaemonSet pods on affected nodes (fast) 2) scale CoreDNS replicas in eu-west cluster from 2->4 (mitigate overload) 3) temporarily set `cache` TTL lower to reduce retries.
kelsey: to restart node-local-dns: `kubectl -n kube-system delete pod node-local-dns-xxxxx --grace-period=0` on each affected node; also set CNI MTU knob to 1500 for nodes that don't need jumbo.
ashok: I pushed a patch to infra playbook to detect mismatched MTU on kubelet start and emit a warning. Filed a follow-up PR to our node-provisioner to ensure GPU RDMA nodes explicitly set `net.mtu=1500` unless operator opts in.
maria: did restart of node-local-dns and scaled CoreDNS fix it?
kelsey: after restarts p95 DNS latency dropped back to ~25ms and error rates returned to normal within ~8 minutes in eu-west-zone-b. No more i/o timeouts in logs.
sre-bot: Incident note: created INC-2026 for 'eu-west DNS timeouts' assigned to ashok, severity low because automated rollback not needed.
ashok: remaining actions: (a) audit nodes for MTU mismatch and report list (b) roll out node-provisioner fix for GPU nodes (c) add alert for node-local-dns pod readiness < 90% in any zone (d) run a DNS resiliency runbook to validate node-local-to-CoreDNS path. I'll take (a) and (b).
maria: I will own (c) and (d). Quick notes for postmortem: - root cause: MTU mismatch on a subset of nodes (9000 vs 1500) leading to UDP DNS fragmentation/loss for node-local-dns -> CoreDNS path; RDMA/SR-IOV nodes made the mismatch more likely due to separate NIC configs. - mitigation: restart node-local-dns, scale CoreDNS, patch node-provisioner. - follow-ups: detect MTU drift, add unit tests for provisioner, add DNS e2e checks in upgrade pipeline.
lee: thumbs up. Also consider fallback to TCP for DNS queries from node-local-dns when UDP retries exceed threshold (CoreDNS supports `prefetch`/`cache` and `forward` with `health` options). Could help if UDP frag is intermittent.
kelsey: added to backlog: prefer TCP on node-local when fragmentation detected.
maria: thanks all, closing this thread once INC-2026 has postmortem attached. :white_check_mark:
